note.question: How do contribution margin differentials affect robust optimization approach to process flexibility designs?
note.overview: The theoretical investigation of the effectiveness of limited flexibility has mainly focused on a performance metric that is based on the maximum sales in units. However, this could lead to substantial profit losses when the maximum sales metric is used to guide flexibility designs while the products have considerably large profit margin differences. The paper addresses this issue by introducing margin differentials into the analysis of process flexibility designs, and our results can provide useful guidelines for the evaluation and design of flexibility configurations when the products have heterogeneous margins.

models.summary: The theoretical investigation of the effectiveness of limited flexibility has mainly focused on a performance metric that is based on the maximum sales in units. However, this could lead to substantial profit losses when the maximum sales metric is used to guide flexibility designs while the products have considerably large profit margin differences. We adopt a robust optimization framework and study process flexibility designs from the worst-case perspective by introducing the dual margin group index (DMGI).
